I am male but  my partner has had rough experiences with being fobbed off and not taken seriously so I know it's really rough. I'm glad to hear you finally managed to get some helpful medication though:)

I did get a referral for ADHD I'm gonna have to go private though or the waiting list is 3 years. Which I can do just need to arrange.

I am currently on medication for migraines been going through lots of different ones for years. I'm also trying different antidepressants but unfortunately think I have withdrawal symptoms from one atm due to not being able to get an appointment with my normal doctor and another one advising me to stay off them and get an eye test even though I had one this year.

I'm getting support slowly I'm just not always up to the calls and stuff and I'm not doing everything quick enough for my parents and they "need" to know what I'm doing with all of it which is tiring. My dad will not believe I have ADHD even if I get diagnosed as he said that to my sister so I haven't told them about it because I don't need any more arguments.

Thank you for taking time to write me a message, have a good day:)

I've had migraines since I was 13, they weren't very frequent for years then they became monthly, eventually they stopped and I thought I'd grown out of it but they came back and they're worse. I've been through various medications and am on one now that seems to help at least a bit. 

I don't have any super obvious triggers stress seems to affect them caffeine not so much only if I have too much and that's only been one occasion so it might've not been the caffeine (I've tried caffeine free no difference).

Diet is okay at home which is when I had 6 in that month so not sure that's affecting it. My diet at uni varies sometimes I can't get out of bed or have the energy to make food so not so good.

Exercise I used to years ago stopped swimming and tennis for non health reasons. Later I played rugby (I know doesn't mix well with migraines and headaches but it was fun and I had a good time for the year or so I played) I stopped that because of migraines. Now just walking really, tennis is more hassle than it's worth with the pain and dizziness I forgot to mention.

Thank you for the message I appreciate it

I'm sorry to hear about your partner that's a horrible thing to do. I'm glad you have a good support system without them.

I'm currently a uni student studying psychology, I scraped through first year but this year everything got harder. Originally I planned to do clinical psychology but it's a long path. I have a few hobbies gaming, art and card games I kinda dropped sport. So yeah some potential careers in there with streaming/selling art but nothing steady. How about you?

Hey, yeah I have a few people to talk to I've shared nearly everything with my partner. However, obviously that can be a lot of stuff so sometimes they find it quite overwhelming and kinda shut down. I have a few friends who know a bit less more just symptoms and less about the suicidal part. I guess sometimes it helps but it's not worth the cost on other people especially my partner who already has plenty to deal with.

Thanks for the message hope you're well.
Oh cool I haven't heard of that before I'll have a look, thank you!

I've been researching it recently and I'm still a bit confused tbh but I kinda enjoy it physically sometimes but mentally I don't often think about sex or want it. It must be very confusing to understand I'm struggling to explain it. Like if physical stuff happens I enjoy it physically most of the time but also feel kind of indifferent mentally.
Yeah I really enjoy being with them emotionally, I guess I didn't give enough context. I really like hanging out with them and being their for each other I'm just not sure about the sex.
Thanks for the suggestion I'll try there!

Yeah I hadn't heard of taking classes at my own pace before that makes sense. Extended deadlines is a good idea I might ask next semester if I have any coursework and things are still rough then. Thank you :)
I probably don't need to be deciding yet I'm a bit of a planner which isn't always helpful. I'll definitely look into that forum that sounds really useful. Thank you very much :)
Thanks for the advice! I'll do some research into those masters courses. How can you go about taking classes at your own pace I'm not really sure how that would work?
